purpose: Owner-requested provisional three-way Texas Phragmites lineage visual lesson; only rights-filtered noncommercial Pages snapshot; do not mark completed or certify Texas lineage.

three_way_roles: North American native subsp. americanus, Michigan source-labelled reference
Introduced Eurasian subsp. australis, Ontario source-labelled reference
Gulf Coast subsp. berlandieri, Florida research-grade source-labelled provisional reference

photo_roles.americanus: Michigan and North Dakota source-described americanus including Matt Lavin close red culm/node (CC BY-SA 2.0); NONE Texas genotype-vouchered. Filename contradictory with author description on North Dakota two photos, document caveat.
photo_roles.australis: Ryan Hodnett CC BY-SA 4.0 Ontario dry stand, physically archived
photo_roles.berlandieri: kdudus CC BY-NC 4.0 Florida reed habitat, individually licensed, user-public noncommercial only
photo_roles.collars_species_only: Stefan.lefnaer species-only European source Phragmites australis leaf sheath/true collar images sl12 (10-mm photographic scale), sl9 (5-mm photographic scale), CC BY-SA 4.0; NOT subspecies or genotype-confirmed. Original image scale does NOT measure individual ligule length automatically.

known_gaps: Current three-way photos are different seasons and locations; never compare density or plume color as lineage proof
Matched old-sheath, exposed culm, true ligule, lower and upper glume photos from independently confirmed lineages not yet archived
Gulf berlandieri observation is research-grade community ID, not molecularly tested
Native-vs-invasive management requires voucher/specialist review and sometimes DNA/haplotype evidence
Future direct mobile overlay inspection and public deployment QA
Native Matt Lavin 2015 source photo filename conflicts with photographer's americanus description; photographed red culms not a certified genotype or Texas voucher.
Austrian Phragmites sl12 and sl9 anatomical photographs are species-level only; no verified Eurasian invasive haplotype or Texas lineage identity from these images.
A close confirmed Gulf Coast berlandieri and introduced Eurasian same-season sheath/culm plus paired real ligule/glume macro with independent lineage voucher/sequence remain outstanding.

rights.license_policy: CC BY-NC 4.0 Gulf reference conditionally allowed only while noncommercial; preserve photographer credit, source, license, modification disclosure. Introduced photo CC BY-SA 4.0.
